messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: Hosted API p99 latency spike detected — sustained queue growth on inference-gpu pool for the last 3m. Autoscaler failing to add GPUs (quota/scale-limit). Marking SEV-2.

alice: Acknowledged. I'm oncall. Quick triage: which customers affected and which model families?

bob: seeing traffic surge from a single heavy tenant and a few noisy public endpoints. Model family: rdl-13b / quantized variants. Autoscaler logs show repeated scale attempts rejected: 
```
ERROR: scale_request_rejected: quota_exceeded (requested_replicas=8, quota=6)
trace: autoscaler/pkg/scale/manager.go:193
```
Also noticed eviction/wait-loop messages where pods stay Pending because GPU capacity is fully reserved.

carol: Confirmed — KV cache pressure is high for rdl-13b long context requests -> higher per-request GPU time. Batching keeps growing latency. Two mitigation paths: 1) reduce per-request concurrency -> early 429s, 2) route tall/long-context requests to smaller model variants or CPU-fallback pool.

alice: Immediate actions: (A) apply emergency throttling rule for public endpoints, (B) enable fallback routing for rdl-13b -> rdl-7b-quantized for non-critical routes, (C) open ticket with infra to increase GPU quota for hosted pool if possible. Bob/Carol can you do A/B now? I’ll page infra.

bob: doing A now. Pushing rate-limit config: 
```yaml
- route: "/v1/generate"
  matcher: "public:*
  throttles:
    - type: token_bucket
      rate: 30rps
      burst: 60
```
Pushed to gateway and warmed routes. Rolling to 3% canary first.

carol: enabling fallback routing in routing-config: 
`fallback_policy: [rdl-13b->rdl-7b-q, rdl-13b->cpu-rt]`
Switching non-authenticated/low-SLO customers to 7b-q. Updating canary to 5% to verify fidelity.

dave: Support: I'm tracking customer impact. So far 4 customers reported timeouts and 2 hitting 502s. Recording affected org IDs and opening outreach for top 2. Any ETA on p99 recovery after throttles?

bob: after throttle and fallback canaries are live: queue depth down ~30% on gateway metrics. p95 improved from 850ms -> 420ms on canary traffic. But global p99 still elevated because autoscaler still can't add GPUs for reserved-heavy tenants.

alice: Good. Next: can we create emergency reserved burst for top customers? If infra can't bump quota, we can temporarily move those tenants to Dedicated reserved pool if they have contracts — route them and mark as paid-burst. Carol, can you draft the route mapping? Eve, FYI for exec/customer comms.

carol: Drafted mapping and created a manual routing override for tenants org-102, org-87: 
```json
{"org-102": "dedicated-us-west-3", "org-87": "dedicated-eu-2"}
```
Applied for org-102; their traffic shifted and latency normalized for that tenant. org-87 is pending dedicated pool capacity check.

bob: infra responded: quota increase request submitted but low chance to get new GPUs within 2 hours (scheduling + procurement). They suggested increasing max_replicas in autoscaler to allow more pods if ephemeral GPUs freed, but current hard quota prevents it. Also showed node-affinity failures in scheduler logs: 
```
Binding failed: InsufficientGPUs. nodes tried: [node-az1, node-az2]
```

alice: OK. Triage conclusion: we cannot rely on autoscaler to fix this quickly. Continue throttles + fallback + pull top-paying tenants to dedicated pools. Also enable early-circuit 429 for long-context requests (context > 8k tokens). Carol please push that rule.

carol: pushed early-circuit rule: 
```sql
IF request.context_tokens > 8000 THEN respond 429 "long request throttled: try shorter context or upgrade plan"
```
Also turned off continuous batching for rdl-13b canary to reduce head-of-line blocking for small queries. Monitoring.

bob: Observability: token-level cost and per-route latency shows small requests now p95 ~200ms, large requests still p99 ~6s for remaining hosts. Queue size trending down after 12m of measures.

dave: Customer update: org-102 confirmed degraded UX resolved after move. org-87 still impacted; they're on standby. Opening status page incident notice now with impact: "degraded for some customers — mitigation in progress. Expected next update in 30m." :loudspeaker: 

eve: Product note: may want to add a short-term guardrail in platform to auto-fallback to quantized variants when queue depth > X. Filing a follow-up feature request and adding to runbook.

alice: Handoff plan: I'm staying for now. If we still have elevated p99 in 30m, I'll escalate to SEV-1 and call for all-hands. For now, owners: bob (infrastructure/scale), carol (runtime/routing), dave (customer comms). Keep updates here every 5-10m.

bob: logging follow-up items: capture full autoscaler trace, scheduler pod binding traces, and per-tenant request profiles. Will post logs link in 10m.

carol: monitoring note: if fallback causes quality regressions, we have rollback knob per-tenant. Also we should enable model-variant circuit on a per-org basis rather than global to preserve SLAs.

dave: posting support thread to affected customers with instructions and interim workaround: shorter contexts or dedicated pool onboarding.

alice: update after 18m: global queue depth down 52%, p99 down from 14s -> 4.2s. Still above acceptable. Leaving throttle rules and fallback in place. Next update 20:30 UTC.

bob: logs posted: https://logs.redwood.internal/alerts/2112345678/autoscaler-traces (private link). Key error repeated: "quota_exceeded" during scaling windows.

incident-bot: NOTE: PagerDuty escalation scheduled in 25m if thresholds persist.

alice: signing off for short break, will be reachable. If p99 drops < 2s and queue stabilizes, we can close SEV-2. Otherwise, escalate. Thanks team. :white_check_mark:
